The association said Ajayi had demonstrated that effective intelligence gathering and national security operations could be pursued without compromising citizens’ fundamental rights, the rule of law and human dignity.
In a statement issued on Friday and signed by its national coordinator, Comrade Emmanuel Nnadozie Onwubiko, HURIWA commended the DSS chief for reviewing inherited security watchlists, addressing cases of prolonged detention and resolving wrongful restrictions imposed on individuals.
It also acknowledged interventions by the DSS leadership in cases involving mistaken identity, wrongful detention and operational errors, including the release of individuals whose continued detention could no longer be justified and compensation for people affected by wrongful security actions.
According to the association, the measures represent significant steps towards building a more accountable, professional and human rights-conscious intelligence institution.
HURIWA noted that although intelligence agencies have enormous responsibilities in protecting national security, such duties must not override the constitutional rights and dignity of citizens.
The organisation urged Ajayi to sustain the reform efforts, strengthen internal accountability mechanisms and ensure that respect for human rights becomes firmly embedded in the operational culture of the service.
Announcing the recognition, HURIWA said the nomination was made by the organised civil rights community under its platform, which it said has a membership of more than 11,000 people worldwide.
The association explained that the award was intended to recognise Ajayi’s leadership and encourage other public officials and security institutions to embrace reforms that place human dignity, justice and accountability at the centre of governance.
It disclosed that the award certificate would be formally presented to the DSS Director-General on December 10, 2026, during its Human Rights Festival to commemorate the 2026 International Human Rights Day.
HURIWA maintained that the performance of an intelligence institution should not be measured solely by its ability to protect national security but also by its commitment to safeguarding the rights, freedoms and dignity of the citizens it serves.
The association also commended President Bola Tinubu for appointing Ajayi to head the DSS, describing him as a competent and professional officer whose leadership had provided an opportunity for institutional reforms.
It congratulated the DSS Director-General on the recognition and urged other public institutions to adopt similar reforms to strengthen democratic governance and accountability.
